numerical_failure.observed_behavior: After the nditer refactor, einsum reductions use NPY_ITER_GROWINNER, so large float64 sums are computed without chunking and lose precision (e.g. np.einsum('i->', np.full(100000000, 1.00000000002)) / 100000000 is less precise than expected; sklearn noticed lower precision).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: einsum reductions should use chunking so large sums keep better precision (GROWINNER removed from the iterator flags in PyArray_EinsteinSum), approximating pairwise-like summation accuracy.
trigger_conditions: einsum reduction over a large array (e.g. 100000000 elements)
iterator uses NPY_ITER_GROWINNER for reductions after the nditer refactor

input_output_examples.expected_output: not given in passages; the test compares against a precision expectation but the exact value is not stated

oracle_clues: test in numpy/_core/tests/test_einsum.py computes res = np.einsum("i->", np.full(num, value)) / num
comment states it is not clear that precision should be guaranteed to this extent
sklearn issue scikit-learn/scikit-learn#30509 reported lower precision

numerical_characteristics.precision: Large float64 sums lose precision when GROWINNER is enabled; the test asserts agreement to decimal=15 for a 1e6-element broadcast sum divided by num, and the code comment says skipping GROWINNER gives a partially stable summation for float64 (pairwise summation would be better). Chunking improves precision of large sums with nonzero mean.
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Large arrays: test uses num = 1_000_000 elements (and a second case with num = 100000000) with value = 1 + eps*8196 or 1.00000000002, where the mean is nonzero.
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: assert_almost_equal with decimal=15 on the mean (res vs value); the passage notes 11 decimals succeed with GROWINNER, larger decimals fail. Comment: 'At with GROWINNER 11 decimals succeed (larger will be less)'.
category_specific_evidence: PR#28043 re-adds chunking in einsum by removing NPY_ITER_GROWINNER from iter_flags in PyArray_EinsteinSum, since the nditer refactor had enabled GROWINNER for reductions and this reduced precision of large sums.
Commit and PR state chunking always improves precision of large sums when their mean is nonzero; scikit-learn (issue #30509) noticed the lower precision.
Performance trade-off: roughly 1% slowdown for the simplest einsum("i,i->i", x, x) case when GROWINNER is not used; the discussion says it is not clear precision should be guaranteed to this extent.
Test in test_einsum.py sums np.broadcast_to of a scalar over 1,000,000 elements, and np.full of 100,000,000 elements with value 1.00000000002, dividing by num to compare to value.
reproduction_risks: Precision outcome depends on whether GROWINNER is active in the nditer, so results differ between the pre- and post-fix builds.
Pairwise summation is suggested as a better fix but is not implemented in the supplied passages.
The test comment states it is unclear the precision should be guaranteed to this extent, so the exact tolerance is not a firm contract.
